samples.summary: The load-bearing regex-shape invariant (no two adjacent whitespace quantifiers, self-closing slash matched by the region) is recorded only in code comments; the canonical subsystem doc's "Sized images" section still describes the old parsing shape and says nothing about the quadratic-backtracking hazard. This repo's own precedent in the same file records exactly this class of constraint at design level — e.g. the mermaid section spells out that the front-matter strip loop is *bounded* because an unbounded one is "quadratic — a stored main-thread freeze for every reader". A future editor tidying `IMG_TAG_RE` back into `(\s[^<>]*?)?\s*\/?>` has no doc-level warning that the shape is deliberate.

samples.summary: The fix quietly widens the accepted syntax beyond what the design doc specifies. Under the old `(\s[^<>]*?)?\s*\/?>` a tag written `` was refused (the stray `/` landed inside the attribute region and `parseAttrs` returned null); the new `IMG_TAG_RE` + `SELF_CLOSE_RE` accepts it, and a new test pins that as intended behavior. The doc only promises `>` vs `/>`. Harmless and arguably more forgiving, but it is unrequested behavior added by a performance fix and now locked in by a test.
